question: In September 2026, the Forum of European Muslim Youth and Student Organisations (FEMYSO) organised its European Action Day against Islamophobia, following the Unite & Act event that had been held during the summer. The latter formed part of the EmpowerAction project, which is carried out within the framework of TACKLE.

TACKLE is supported by the Commission’s DEAR programme and comprises a system, managed by Avocats sans frontières, via which grants are awarded to third parties. In the report ‘Frères musulmans et islamisme politique en France’ (‘The Muslim Brotherhood and Political Islamism in France’), published by France’s Ministry of the Interior, FEMYSO is described as part of the Muslim Brotherhood.

In October 2025, France, Austria and the Netherlands also called on the Council to strengthen the traceability and monitoring of EU funding, to prevent European funds from benefiting organisations with links to Islamism or antisemitism. 1.
Did Unite & Act receive funds, directly or indirectly, from the DEAR programme via TACKLE and Avocats sans frontières?
What was the precise amount of EU funding awarded and paid to FEMYSO within the framework of EmpowerAction?
Why does the Commission not see the Muslim Brotherhood and related organisations that aim to bring about the Islamisation of Europe as a threat?
